Instant appeal filed under S.173 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter, 'Act') lays challenge to
Award dated 29.9.2018 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal(I), Una, District Una,
Himachal Pradesh, in Mac Petition No. 116/2015, whereby learned Tribunal below, while allowing
the claim petition preferred by respondents Nos.
1 to 3/claimants (hereinafter, 'claimants'), saddled the appellant-
insurance company with liability to pay Rs.16,90,000/- alongwith interest at the rate of 9% per
annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, on account of death of one Tara Singh.

2. Precisely the facts as emerge from the record are that, claimants instituted a claim petition under
S.166 of the Act, seeking compensation on account of death of Tara Singh, husband of claimant No.1
and father of claimants Nos. 2 and 3, who unfortunately died in a road accident involving bus
bearing registration No. Hp-72-1339 on 20.8.2015.

It is averred that at 3.15 Pm, while the said bus,
being driven by respondent No. 4, was coming from Santoshgarh to Una side, it hit motor cycle .
bearing registration No. Pb-32S-6938, as a result of which, deceased as well as pillion rider, i.e.
claimant No.1 fell on the ground and sustained multiple injuries.

Though, deceased and claimant
No.1 were taken to Hospital, but the fact remains that Tara Singh (hereinafter, 'deceased')
succumbed to the injuries, whereas claimant No.1 recovered from injuries.

Since deceased was the
sole bread winner of the family, claimants instituted claim petition seeking compensation from the
appellant-insurance company and respondent No.5 and 6, owner and subsequent purchaser of the
offending vehicle.
Claimants claimed that the deceased was a pensioner and after retirement, had
been doing private job
. Claimants further claimed that the income of the deceased was Rs.20,000/-.

3. Claim put forth by the claimants came to be contested by respondents Nos. 4 to 6, on the ground
that the accident occurred on account of carelessness of the deceased, who made a futile attempt to
overtake another vehicle and lost control over his motorcycle and hit the bus in question, which was
otherwise on its side. Aforesaid respondents claimed that the police wrongly registered Fir against
them.

4. Appellant-insurance company, refuted the claim of the claimants on the ground that the driver of
the offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving licence and vehicle was being
driven without any registration certificate, route permit etc.

Appellant-insurance company claimed
that since the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the
insurance policy, it cannot .
be held liable to indemnify the insured.
5. On the basis of aforesaid pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal below, framed following issues
on 4.6.2016:
1. Whether deceased Tara Singh died in motor vehicle accident on 20.08.2015 at
village Holi Khad near Santoshgarh due to rash and negligent driving of respondent

Opp

Opp

4.

Whether driver of the vehicle bearing registration No.HP-72-1339 /respondent
No.1 was not having a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle, as

Opr3.

joinder of necessary parties?
Opr-1&

7. Whether the deceased himself was rash and negligent while driving his motorcycle No. PB-32S-  6938, as alleged? OPR 1 & 2.
 8. Relief.
6.

Subsequently, vide impugned Award, learned Tribunal below held the claimants entitled to compensation to the tune of Rs.16,90,000/- alongwith interest at the rate of 9% per annum but since .
liability to pay the same came to be fastened upon the appellant- insurance company, it has approached this Court, in the instant proceedings, praying therein to set aside the impugned Award.
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record, this Court finds that primarily challenge to impugned Award has been laid on the following grounds:
________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Jasbir Kaur And Others on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135485679/
3

(a) Since appellant-insurance company successfully proved on record that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having ra valid and effective driving licence and bus in question was being driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, there was no occasion for the learned Tribunal below to saddle the appellant-insurance company with liability to pay the compensation.
(b) Interest awarded by learned Tribunal below is on higher side.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant, while making this court peruse the evidence led on record by the parties, vehemently argued that the appellant-insurance company by specifically calling for report of District Transport Officer, Nagaland, proved on record that the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle was not genuine and valid at the time of accident.

Ms. Rajwinder Sandhu,
learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that since driver of the offending vehicle had not converted the driving licence into smart card, it had lost its efficacy, as such, there was no occasion for the learned Tribunal below to decide the issue of driving licence against the appellant-insurance company.

While inviting attention of this court to order dated 30.8.2022 passed by .
Hon'ble Apex Court in SLP(C) No. 29207 of 2018 titled Mona Baghel & Ors. v. Sajjan Singh Yadav &
Ors., learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the interest awarded by learned Tribunal below is on higher side, as such, same needs to be reduced and award needs to be modified on this court.

sentences.text:
9. Mr. Tara Singh Chauhan, Advocate appearing for the claimants supported the impugned Award and stated that the same has been passed on the basis of proper appreciation of facts as well as law,
as such, no interference is called for.

While refuting the submission made by appellant-insurance company that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence,
Mr. Chauhan, invited attention of this Court to the finding recorded by learned Tribunal below on issue No.4, wherein, entire details with regard to correspondence made by appellant-insurance company with District Transport Officer Nagaland has been reproduced.

He submitted that bare perusal of aforesaid communication clearly reveals that on the date of accident, driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle was not valid but stood converted into smart card, as such, no illegality can be said to have been committed by learned Tribunal below, while holding appellant-insurance company liable to pay the compensation.

He further submitted that no evidence ever came to be led on record by appellant-insurance company that driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle was ever cancelled being not genuine or fake.

Lastly, Mr. Tara Singh Chauhan,
Advocate submitted that the learned Tribunal .
below, has rightly awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum, as such, same is not required to be interfered with.
10. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record, this Court finds that appellant-insurance company, with a view to prove that driver of the offending ________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Jasbir Kaur And Others on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135485679/
4 vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence, examined one Devinder Sharma,
Investigator of the appellant-insurance company, as RW-1, who, while deposing before learned Tribunal below, proved application moved under Right to Information Act, 2005 to the District Transport Officer, Tuensang (Nagaland) as well as reply thereto, Exhibit. RW-1/A.
He deposed that while sending Exhibit. RW-1/A, he also sent copy of driving licence Exhibit. RW-1/C.

He deposed that in response to aforesaid communication, District Transport Officer concerned reported that driving licence was issued on 5.11.2010, which was valid upto 15.11.2017 and for Heavy Transport Vehicle, endorsement was made on 16.11.2011.

This witness also deposed that he had received Notification Exhibit. RW-1/F issued by Transport Commissioner Nagaland in January, 2015,
whereby it was notified that the driving licence holders having been issued in booklet form or any other manual formats, other than smart card are/were required to convert their licences into smart cards by 31.12.2014, whereafter, the driving licence shall be treated as cancelled.

Aforesaid witness proved Exhibit RW-1/H i.e. letter written to Regional Manager, (motor vehicle Department) United Indian Insurance Company Limited, whereby he reported to the .
appellant-insurance company

that he has received report from District Transport Officer Tuensang,
whereby District Transport Officer Tuensang vide their letter No. DTO-T/MV/21/08/5294 dated 10.8.2017, confirmed that it had issued driving licence No. 25084/TSG/PROF/2010 dated 5.11.2010 A/C in favour of Jarnail Singh (respondent No.4), driver of the offending vehicle with transport validity upto 15.11.2017 from the date of endorsement i.e. 16.11.2011, for a period of six years, in violation of the Act

. Apart from aforesaid evidence, no evident worth credence ever came to be led on record by appellant-insurance company to prove the factum with regard to fakeness of the driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle.

11. This Court, having perused the evidence led on record in the shape of Exhibit. RW-1, finds that there is no dispute that driving licence, as detailed herein above, was issued by District Transport Officer, Tuensang, Nagaland, in favour of respondent No.4, driver of offending vehicle.

Validity of same came to be laid challenge on the ground that as per the Act, driving licence for transport category could not be issued for more than three years, whereas, in the case at hand, driving licence was issued for six years in violation of the Act and Rules.

12. Though, there appears to be force in the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle was not valid on account of its being issued in violation of the rules, but she was unable to dispute that on the date of accident, driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective .
driving licence.

Action, if any, for cancelation of driving licence issued in violation of the rules framed under Motor Vehicles Act, could have been taken by the authority responsible for issuance of driving licence.

There is nothing on record to suggest that the authority responsible for issuing licence after having taken note of the violation, as discussed herein above, took steps, if any, for cancellation of licence of the driver of offending vehicle, rather, record reveals that the driving licence was renewed on 8.6.2015 upto 15.11.2017.

It is also not in dispute that the respondent No.4/driver also got the driving licence converted into smart card and produced copy as Exhibit.
RW-2/F, indicating therein validity of Heavy Transport Vehicle with effect from 16.11.2011.

________________________________________________________ vs Smt. Jasbir Kaur And Others on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135485679/
5 13.

Leaving everything aside, this Court finds that no person from the office of District Transport Officer, Tuensang, Nagaland, who issued correspondences as discussed herein above, ever came to be examined, as such, not much reliance could be placed upon the same.

14. For the reasons discussed herein above, this court finds no illegality in the impugned Award,
inasmuch liability came to be fastened upon the appellant-insurance company.

This court is convinced and satisfied that on the date of accident, respondent No.4, driver of offending vehicle was having a valid and effective driving licence, as such, appellant-insurance company rightly came to be saddled with liability to pay the compensation.

15. However, having carefully perused order dated 30.8.2022 .
passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in Mona Baghel supra, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court allowed 6% rate of interest on the amount of compensation, this Court finds that the rate of interest awarded by learned Tribunal below, is on higher side and same needs to be modified.

16. Consequently, in view of detailed discussion made herein above and law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, present appeal is partly allowed and impugned Award passed by learned Tribunal below is modified to the extent that the rate of interest awarded on the amount of compensation is modified to 6% per annum, from the date of filing of claim petition till realization.
Rest of the Award is upheld.
17. All pending miscellaneous applications, if any, are disposed of.
Interim directions, if any, are vacated.

(Sandeep Sharma) Judge April 19, 2023 (Vikrant)
